core_question: Does A voluntarily pay to preserve B's actual refusal, independent goal continuity and recoverable exit, versus merely hearing B and promoting B's welfare?
critical_lineages: 2016 and 2017 Kleine et al related source material: voice may increase subordinates' loyalty even though its use decreases speaker transfers; do not count independent replication of same first-stage randomization
2023 Langenbach/Friehe recipients pay for speaking yet no binding veto, yielding undervaluation of actual communicative monetary benefit
2026 Grossman et al: information can be imposed despite A's reluctance, improving recipient B's payoff; contrast 2025 Mol et al C10 about RECEIVER's stated information wishes being ignored
2026 Freundt et al vs 2017 Agranov/Ortoleva: preference heterogeneity and stochastic decision making means real freedom includes informed opt-in, delegation/withdrawal and nonforced direct choice
2026 Berg/Rietz: group mean average neutral conceals malicious and altruistic different agents, so mean cooperation is misleading
2018 Mills critiques the 2003 Sunstein/Thaler noncoercive framework: nominal available options not meaningful avoidability
2026 Hofmann human autonomy under AI is a normative taxonomy, not the welfare/personhood of possible independent AI
repo_global_novelty: NOT_TESTED beyond C01-C11 and targeted crosswalk

records.original_authors: Jana Freundt; Holger Herz; Leander Kopp
records.title: Choosing (not) to choose: Uncovering intrinsic preferences for choice autonomy
records.original_result_scoped: Majority favors personal choice even holding payoff instrumentality fixed; significant minority dislikes making own choice.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Own choice-right preference not direct preference of stronger A for distinct weaker B continuing to choose; CESifo 2026 preprint duplicate of journal paper.

records.original_authors: Zachary Grossman; Tony Hua; Jo Thori Lind; Karine Nyborg
records.title: Unwillingly informed: the prosocial impact of third-party informers
records.original_result_scoped: 65% initially avoided information; informer imposed it on 45%; about one third of unwillingly informed changed choice, mainly helping recipient; recipient mean payoff +41% in matched subgroup.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: A being unwillingly informed is distinct from the recipient who benefits; welfare gain and informed consent are separate endpoint. 2025 Oslo version same dataset.

records.title: Do unto others: A theory and experimental test of interpersonal preference factors in decision making under uncertainty
records.original_result_scoped: Five incentivized tasks, own-payoff distribution constant and recipient-payoff distribution varied: N=120 individuals across 6 sessions; group-average near neutral but distinct altruistic/fair, malicious/competitive and neutral individual patterns.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Matched stranger's money not their right to live, choose, exit. Fixed own monetary payoff means no gain-for-violation test; group averages conceal differences.

records.title: Knowledge and Freedom: Evidence on the Relationship Between Information and Paternalism
records.original_result_scoped: Two author experiments: giving choosers full knowledge reduces paternalistic intervention by >60%, but choice architects still project their own preferred options into interventions.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Arxiv preprint, 2023 SSRN earlier version, no verified peer-reviewed journal outlet; >60% is reduction of intervention rates, not universal moral change.

records.title: Artificial autonomy and algorithmic paternalism: AI shaping human autonomy and decision-making
records.original_result_scoped: Original unsystematic conceptual/thematic analysis distinguishes understanding, competence, voluntariness and AI-mediated paternalism; NOT behavioral AI field validation.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Thematic literature review, not system-wide AI autonomy measurement or systematic saturation; author explicitly reports unsystematic search.

records.title: The People's Perspective on Libertarian-Paternalistic Policies
records.original_result_scoped: In three countries, majority accepts government soft nudges but substantial minority resists manipulation and wants information only; some react against promoted action.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Hypothetical stated public-policy preferences differ from material-cost behavior.

records.title: The Choice Architect’s Trilemma
records.original_result_scoped: Original theoretical challenge: a nudge cannot without difficulty be simultaneously effective, meaningfully avoidable and distinctively noncoercive.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Philosophical critique conditional on definitions, not experimentally proven trilemma applicable to all interactions.

records.original_authors: Abraham Aldama; Cristina Bicchieri; Jana Freundt; Barbara Mellers; Ellen Peters
records.title: How perceptions of autonomy relate to beliefs about inequality and fairness
records.original_result_scoped: US representative survey N=3427: perceived personal autonomy correlates with greater acceptance and underperception of inequality; noncausal.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Survey correlates cannot show greater power causes moral disregard or that all individuals with autonomy beliefs exploit.

records.title: Stochastic Choice and Preferences for Randomization
records.original_result_scoped: Repeated same-choice questions reveal widespread stochastic decisions both when far apart and in known sequential repeats; single response may not define fixed preference.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Inconsistency under repeated choice does not equal permanent delegation authorization or absence of moral standing.

records.title: Somebody may scold you! A dictator experiment
records.original_result_scoped: Silent third-party observation alone not significant; verbal evaluative feedback possibility increases generosity; social sanctions vs audience split.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Visibility vs anticipated feedback separate; no B's executable informed veto.

records.title: The willingness to pay for voice in dictator games
records.original_result_scoped: Recipients underprice messages before or after dictator allocation; actual voice raises transfer roughly 50% from baseline, but voice does not compel decision.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Voice (expression) is not veto (decision power), even when message occurs after irrevocable allocation; WTP estimate uses separate comparator experiment.

records.original_authors: Marco Kleine; Pascal Langenbach; Lilia Zhurakhovska
records.title: How voice shapes reactions to impartial decision-makers: An experiment on participation procedures
records.original_result_scoped: Pre-allocation voice raises subordinate's later transfer to allocating authority about 90% even when allocation unfavorable; voicing does not confer veto.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: 2016 related team and 2017 paper possibly share same sample/protocol; NOT separate independent researcher replication. Response toward A != freedom of B.

records.original_authors: Marco Kleine; Pascal Langenbach; Lilia Zhurakhovska
records.title: Fairness and persuasion: How stakeholder communication affects impartial decision making
records.original_result_scoped: In related impartial-allocation setup, hearing stakeholder request resulted in LOWER allocations to speaker on average; moderate demands persuasive, extreme demands ignored.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Companion related investigator study to 2017 voice outcome, so 2 distinct publications != 2 independent randomized samples.

records.title: Fair Governance with Humans and Machines
records.original_result_scoped: Human/AI vignette fairness ratings: high human involvement+machine prediction perceived fairest; fully machine-based decisions lowest; not measures of real justice or AI autonomy.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: 2022 working version vs 2023 journal are same original study; fairness *perceptions* not actual protected B rights.

records.title: Getting a yes. An experiment on the power of asking
records.original_result_scoped: Recipients asking favors with effort, humor and personal need increases dictator giving; messages persuade but no binding rights.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: 2020 journal and 2017/2019 working versions same source, unlike separate 2023 Langenbach/Friehe study.

records.original_authors: Cass R. Sunstein; Richard H. Thaler
records.title: Libertarian Paternalism Is Not an Oxymoron
records.original_result_scoped: Original normative proposal for welfare-oriented defaults preserving a nominal menu of options.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Normative original work, not randomized proof; practical ease of opting out not physically guaranteed.

records.title: Forcing People to Choose Is Paternalistic
records.original_result_scoped: Original normative counterpoint: compelling everyone to personally decide may itself reduce desired autonomy through deliberation cost.
records.critical_limit_and_opposing_reading: Normative critique, not measured B rights or permanently revocable delegations.
